_comment: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT FIXTURE, not a source of truth. Terraform declares the realm and the
organizations; this fills in what Keycloak treats as runtime: each organization's groups,
the roles mapped onto them, users, and who belongs where.
Group names are the organization's own data and differ per organization on purpose: an
application reads roles, never group names. Only `kanzo-conformance` roles are mapped here;
an application maps its own roles onto these groups from its own repository.
`Research`, `Research/ML` and `Finance` hold no role: they are what an application grants to
by id (keasy's "Research may use this"). acme and globex each have a `Research`, with two ids.
`bruno` is in acme's `Research/ML`, so his token carries Research's id too (inherited).
`gil` is in five of acme's groups, past the conformance client's overage threshold of 4.
`ana` belongs to TWO organizations, so switching and `organization:*` can be exercised.
`fede` belongs to acme with no group, so holding no role there is a state to test.
`dan` belongs to none and holds a client role directly: the single-tenant shape.
